findings.highlight: everyone would have been quiet after our performance
findings.evidenceJa: 外したら、あとずっと静まっちゃいそうで
findings.explanation: Setsuna feared that if their old opening number failed to land, the audience would remain subdued for everything that followed. The English moves the silence to after the entire performance, removing the risk attached to opening their set with this particular song.
findings.japanese:
「本当は、最初にこの曲を持ってくるのって、
結構勇気がいったんですよ。古い曲だし…
外したら、あとずっと静まっちゃいそうで」
findings.todokanai: "To tell you the truth, when we first thought of using this song, it took a lot of courage to decide on it because it's a pretty old song… If we'd messed up, everyone would have been quiet after our performance."

findings.highlight: "Standing here and singing in front of everyone… I've never been this nervous in my entire life."
findings.evidenceJa:
「こういうところに立って歌うの、
ホント生まれて初めてなので凄く緊張してました」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says this is her first time singing in a place like this and that she was very nervous; the English replaces the first-time fact with a lifetime superlative about nervousness.
findings.japanese:
「こういうところに立って歌うの、
ホント生まれて初めてなので凄く緊張してました」
findings.todokanai: "Standing here and singing in front of everyone… I've never been this nervous in my entire life."

findings.highlight: more than good enough for this
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that Setsuna has composure to spare: she is relaxed enough onstage to improvise this speech. The English instead praises her general ability, losing the immediate evidence that her stage fright has vanished.
findings.todokanai: You're actually more than good enough for this, Setsuna…

findings.highlight: was the head of the festival committee
findings.evidenceJa: 学園祭実行委員とか、クラス委員とか色々なお仕事を兼任してるので
findings.explanation: Setsuna lists festival-committee work, class-representative work, and Haruki's other concurrent jobs. The Japanese never calls him head of the festival committee; the English invents a leadership post and shifts the ongoing accumulation of duties into the past.
findings.japanese:
「北原くんは、学園祭実行委員とか、
クラス委員とか色々なお仕事を兼任してるので、
お世話になった方も多いと思います」
findings.todokanai: "In the past, Kitahara-kun was the head of the festival committee and he was also a class representative. He's been involved with a lot of things at school, so I'm sure he's had many opportunities to help you all out with all sorts of things."

findings.highlight: supporting us through his two-faced nature
findings.evidenceJa: 陰ひなたから支えてくれる
findings.explanation: 陰ひなたなく/陰ひなたから支える means supporting someone both publicly and behind the scenes. Todokanai TL reads the light-and-shadow idiom as duplicity, making Setsuna call dependable Haruki two-faced in the middle of praising him.
findings.japanese:
「普段と同様、いつもわたしたちメンバーを、
陰ひなたから支えてくれる、
とても頼りがいのある人です」
findings.todokanai: "And just as he's done for many of you, he was the one driving us on and supporting us through his two-faced nature. He's someone that we could always depend on."

findings.highlight: When she joined our group, we were amazed by just how skilled she was
findings.evidenceJa: わたしたちのユニットに参加してくれたのが不思議なくらい実力がずば抜けてて
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Kazusa is so far beyond them that it is almost strange she agreed to join their band at all. The English merely says her skill amazed them after she joined, deleting the affectionate self-deprecation about how absurdly overqualified she is.
findings.japanese:
「わたしたちのユニットに参加してくれたのが
不思議なくらい実力がずば抜けてて、
何度助けられたか、もう数えきれません」
findings.todokanai: "When she joined our group, we were amazed by just how skilled she was. I can't even tell you how many times she's helped us already!"

findings.highlight: I was told to delete the bass programming and do the keyboard instead
findings.evidenceJa: ベース外してキーボード入れろって
findings.explanation: Takeya is reporting Haruki's audacious arrangement instruction: take the bass out of Sound of Destiny and put the keyboard in. The English turns it into something Takeya himself was ordered to do to programmed audio, inventing both the performer and the implementation.
findings.japanese:
「で、『ＳＯＵＮＤ　ＯＦ　ＤＥＳＴＩＮＹ』は、
ベース外してキーボード入れろって…」
findings.todokanai: "And for Sound of Destiny, I was told to delete the bass programming and do the keyboard instead…"

findings.highlight: she went along with it so easily
findings.evidenceJa: それでも簡単にやっちゃうところが
findings.explanation: Io's complaint is that Kazusa can execute the technically absurd arrangement with ease. “Went along with it” makes the feat one of willing compliance instead of effortless musical ability, breaking the punch line to their exchange about her detestable genius.
findings.japanese:
「それでも簡単にやっちゃうところが、
思いっきり嫌味なんだけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "But the fact that she went along with it so easily is what makes it so detestable."

findings.highlight: couldn't care less what anyone thinks of her
findings.evidenceJa: 自らが好むと好まざるとに関わらず
findings.explanation: Kazusa draws the room's eyes whether she likes it or not. Todokanai TL changes involuntary visibility into an assertion that she does not care what anyone thinks, replacing the scene's external dynamic with a much harder claim about her attitude.
findings.japanese:
ステージの上の黒いピエロは、
自らが好むと好まざるとに関わらず、
会場の目を次々と自分に向けさせていた。
findings.todokanai: The audience's full attention is now on the clown dressed in black on top of the stage, who couldn't care less what anyone thinks of her.

findings.highlight: she just thinks it'd be cuter if I made a fool of myself
findings.evidenceJa: 馬鹿な弟子ほど可愛いの法則なのか
findings.explanation: Haruki jokingly invokes a proverb-like rule that the more foolish the pupil, the dearer the pupil becomes. The English instead says Kazusa wants him to make a fool of himself, changing her indulgent attachment to her hopeless student into a desire to see him embarrassed.
findings.japanese:
…のに、全然効きやしない。
俺の師匠は、本当に弟子のことを信用してないのか、
それとも、馬鹿な弟子ほど可愛いの法則なのか。
findings.todokanai: But it's not really reassuring. Looks like my master really can't trust her disciple, or she just thinks it'd be cuter if I made a fool of myself.

findings.evidenceJa: まともに評価なんかできるわけない俺たちのステージ
findings.explanation: Haruki says their stage cannot be evaluated fairly because the understaffed band is using a backing track and repeatedly deploying crowd-pleasing cheat moves. Todokanai TL converts that refusal of fair comparison into Haruki judging the performance itself shallow.
findings.japanese:
人が足りないから、オケも使ってる。
受けを狙って、反則技を何度も繰り出してる。
まともに評価なんかできるわけない俺たちのステージ。
findings.todokanai: Since we're short on people, we're using pre-recorded segmentsーa rather underhanded method. As a whole, our performance is pretty shallow.

findings.highlight: there were a few hiccups in the singing
findings.evidenceJa: 適当だったり声詰まらせたりして
findings.explanation: The preceding line identifies both Kazusa's bass and Setsuna's vocals. Haruki then says Kazusa was playing roughly and Setsuna's voice was catching; Todokanai TL retains only the vocal hiccups, omitting Kazusa's part of the deliberately paired underperformance.
findings.japanese:
二人とも、視線が泳いでたり、
適当だったり声詰まらせたりして、
じっくり聴いてみれば結構酷いものになってるはずだ。
findings.todokanai: With the way both of their gazes were wandering, and how there were a few hiccups in the singing, it would probably sound pretty bad to anyone listening closely.

findings.explanation: 凛とした describes Kazusa's dignified, resolute bearing as she wordlessly tells Haruki to trust Setsuna. Calling it cold changes supportive confidence into emotional distance at the point where the three musicians coordinate without speech.
findings.japanese: その凛とした表情が俺に言葉以外で告げてくる。
findings.todokanai: That cold expression tells me everything I need to know.

findings.highlight: we gave the audience one last awkward bow and left the stage
findings.evidenceJa: ぎこちない挨拶で別れた
findings.explanation: Thirty minutes earlier, the three band members awkwardly said goodbye to one another, concealing their embarrassment after clearing out. Todokanai TL invents a final bow to the audience and repeats their departure from the stage, erasing the private post-performance parting.
findings.japanese:
なんだか照れくささを隠すように、
ぎこちない挨拶で別れたのが３０分前。
findings.todokanai: As if hiding our embarrassment, we gave the audience one last awkward bow and left the stage. All that, just some half an hour ago.

findings.evidenceJa: 『お帰りなさいませ』とか言ってくれる
findings.explanation: お帰りなさいませ is the marked maid-cafe welcome-home formula, which is why the dazzling singer immediately serving classmates has such charge. The generic “Welcome” removes the roleplay register and the cultural joke rather than translating it.
findings.japanese:
さっきまでステージの上で輝いていた雪菜のままで、
目の前で『お帰りなさいませ』とか言ってくれる訳で。
findings.todokanai: I'd bet everyone would want to hear her say, "Welcome" just for them, right after her dazzling performance on the stage.

findings.highlight: if my brain were working properly
findings.evidenceJa: 脳に知れたら絶対に放送禁止だ
findings.explanation: Haruki personifies his brain as a censor: if it found out he was saying something this painfully earnest, it would ban the line from broadcast. Todokanai TL replaces that joke with the ordinary claim that he would not speak this way while thinking clearly.
findings.japanese:
だって、こんな痛い台詞、
脳に知れたら絶対に放送禁止だ。
findings.todokanai: Because I know full well I'd never say something as embarrassing as this if my brain were working properly.

findings.evidenceJa: あいつは“花”で、あたしは“奴”か
findings.explanation: Kazusa explicitly contrasts Haruki's elevated metaphor for Setsuna, “flower,” with the rough 奴 he used for Kazusa. “Person” is neutral English and erases the entire lexical contrast she has noticed between how he casts the two women.
findings.japanese: 『あいつは“花”で、あたしは“奴”か…』
findings.todokanai: "So she's a 'flower,' and I'm just a 'person,' huh…?"

findings.highlight: There's no way I wasn't happy
findings.evidenceJa: 嬉しくないわけないだろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa insists there is no way she is not happy to be with Haruki and Setsuna. The English abruptly puts the final and most vulnerable admission in the past, making it possible to read her happiness as something already over rather than an ongoing feeling she is struggling to voice.
findings.japanese:
『………嫌なわけないだろ。
楽しくないわけないだろ。
嬉しくないわけないだろ』
findings.todokanai: "…There's no way I wouldn't like it. There's no way it wouldn't be fun. There's no way I wasn't happy."
